newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sharp rise seen in southwestern France maize crop.
newsitem.headline: Sharp rise seen in southwestern France maize crop.

text.p: With the first maize cuttings due to start by mid-September in France's southwest, crop analysts are already predicting a 15 percent jump in output for the Aquitaine region over last year.
But they also cautioned cooler temperatures over the last two weeks were slowing down the maturing process.
An analyst for the local ONIC grain office in Bordeaux estimated the regional yield might reach 1993's record level of 8.6 tonnes per hectare against 8.0 tonnes last year.
This would put the 1996 crop at 3.2 million tonnes against 2.8 million last year.
ONIC also expects maize area to rise to 370,000 hectares from 355,000 hectares.
Analysts said the crop benefited from good moisture levels and was generally healthy in the absence of disease.
The only sore spot was non-irrigated maize in the Dordogne area which apparently suffered from a lack of moisture, the analyst said, but did not provide further details.
The first cuttings are expected to start around September 15, some 10 days ahead of schedule, in the Landes region near the Atlantic coast.
